tb21_profile.skill: Debug a memory-corruption regression in a C runtime's heap/free-list bookkeeping inside a large self-hosting codebase, then rebuild and run its own test suite
tb21_profile.domain: OCaml runtime internals in C: major-heap sweeping, free lists, compiler bootstrap, make-based build
tb21_profile.task_form: find-and-patch-a-regression in a large native project, verified by the project's own build+testsuite

verifier_notes: Nothing overturned. Checked grades for the CalibForge picks: se_20260604_003814_004 is graded weak but its suite drives an allocator through stress patterns, so it is not vacuous; se_20260604_003113_014 (Lisp GC) is graded ok and is the single closest task in the whole pool. TerminalWorld's two best-matching entries (tw_245032 openal-soft segfault, tw_226228 OCaml/ocamlbuild) are both FREE, so they are ranked in per_source but excluded from final_top10.
searches: tools.py search rebench '(?i)segfault|segmentation fault|refcount|use-after-free|memory leak|core dump'
tools.py search smith '(?i)segfault|segmentation fault|refcount|memory leak|recursion|stack overflow'
tools.py search rebench '(?i)\bcython|C extension|compile to C|codegen|transpil'

TMax-15K.reason: Repair a broken Makefile, then find the memory bug that crashes the C binary on a malformed payload - same build-then-debug-crash loop.
Bisect a git history to find the regression that makes a C++ daemon core-dump, then patch it; identical genre to the broken-GC-commit hunt.
C server segfaults only under -O3: forces reasoning about undefined behaviour and memory layout rather than reading an error message.
Fix a buffer-size miscalculation in urldecode.c that corrupts the heap - same pointer-arithmetic-on-a-heap-block reasoning.
Off-by-one allocation causing heap corruption in a C server; off-by-one in block accounting is exactly the OCaml free-list failure mode.
Use-after-free in a C++ interpreter for a build DSL: object lifetime bugs in an interpreter, plus getting the build working.
Diagnose a C++ crash from the one input that triggers it, using the crash artefacts - the same evidence-to-root-cause path.
Track a leak in a C service triggered only by one malformed record class; teaches allocation/free accounting, not GC internals.
main is broken twice over: build config fails, and once built the engine misbehaves - mirrors fix-the-build-then-fix-the-bug.
Repair build/env so the project compiles, then profile and fix a linear memory leak; Go rather than C runtime.

Recursive-Task-Synthesis.reason: Only real OCaml in this corpus: writes .ml source and an ocamlbuild Makefile, so it teaches the OCaml toolchain but no debugging.
OCaml QCheck build driven by a README-described profile; same toolchain exposure, slightly more configuration reading.
OCaml/ocamlbuild again, with templates to locate and a placeholder to complete; closest RTS gets to the OCaml build system.
Build a crash-prone C binary from its Makefile and drive GDB against the crashing input - build plus native crash analysis.
Same buggy-png family: compile from source, pick a GDB profile, capture the crash - transfers the native-debugger habit only.
Third buggy-png variant; adds crafted-input selection but still reports a crash rather than fixing the code.
Fix wrong ARM64 assembly output and author the missing Makefile: low-level correctness plus build authoring, tiny scale.
Multi-file C program driven through an existing build system; exercises make/linking only, no debugging.
Two-stage Makefile build plus make clean; build-system literacy, nothing about memory or crashes.
Compile a C program and match reference output; mostly the /app report boilerplate this corpus repeats.

TerminalWorld-Seeds-Clean.reason: Fix a real segfault in openal-soft's C init loop over a static backend list; closest here, but FREE-graded so barred from top10.
The only OCaml/ocamlbuild task in this corpus; domain match only, and its suite is FREE.
Build Git from source on a remote host: driving a large C project's configure/make, which fix-ocaml-gc also demands.
Clone and build the Tcl interpreter from its unix/ tree with a prefix; language-runtime build practice, no debugging.
Compile the SCTK C toolkit from a repo and install it; build-from-source only.
Resolve missing build dependencies on CentOS then build from source - the environment-repair half of the TB task.
Write a fork/execvp shell in C; systems C practice but nothing about heaps or regressions.
Run a crashing binary under GDB and capture the backtrace and maps; observation only, and FREE-graded.
Demonstrates a C preprocessor trick; same toolchain vocabulary, no bug to find.
Clone, cmake build, make test, run binary - pure build boilerplate and FREE-graded.

SWE-Smith-Seeds-Clean.reason: Wrong C++ standard flags emitted for gcc/clang; reasoning about compiler invocation is the ecosystem fix-ocaml-gc lives in.
Compiler-variable resolution broken when cross-building; toolchain/build-config debugging after a rewrite.
AutotoolsToolchain mishandles compiler flags - same autotools/make world the OCaml bootstrap is built with.
Async-generator finalization during collection: reasoning about when a runtime reclaims an object, the GC-semantics half of the task.
Broken run-length decoder; the TB bug is in run-length-compressed free space, so RLE length/offset accounting transfers a little.
Deeply nested input blows the stack after a rewrite; teaches recursion-depth failure analysis, not heap accounting.
Emit a jobs parameter so cmake builds in parallel; build-system configuration, no debugging depth.
Stale subsettings after a compiler setting changes: invalidation bookkeeping bug, mildly analogous to stale free-list state.
Removed serialization helpers break every SFTP op; trace a wide failure back to one missing primitive.
Reverse line iteration with buffer/offset arithmetic gone wrong; offset bookkeeping, but in Python on a file, not a heap.

SWE-Rebench-Tasks-Clean.reason: Interpreter segfaults inside garbage collection; issue is worked from gdb backtraces, the same evidence the OCaml crash gives.
Extend a Python-to-C compiler's backend to return dicts: code generation plus C memory ownership decisions.
Crash inside the codegen printer; debugging a compiler pipeline from a traceback into the printer stage.
Pyccel fails while invoking the C compiler on a generated module - build-tool integration failure inside a compiler.
Template handling bug in the same Python-to-C compiler; compiler-internals domain, ordinary logic fix.
Memory-profiler CLI clobbers argv; memory-tooling ecosystem, but the fix touches no allocator logic.
Unbounded growth in CookieJar: find the structure that is never pruned, the same question as free space never reclaimed.
Second fix for the same CookieJar leak; duplicate skill, kept for the reclamation-bookkeeping pattern.
Cython wrapper over a C http-parser behaving wrongly; crossing the Python/C boundary to locate blame.
Cython binding to the HDF5 C library misbehaves with file locking off; native-library binding debugging.

Terminal-Lego-15k.reason: C++ program correct at -O0 and broken at -O2 from an out-of-bounds write; exactly the class of latent memory bug a hand-edited GC produces.
Three buggy C programs to diagnose and fix from the command line; pinned tests and real find-the-bug work.
Use valgrind to locate and fix leaks and invalid accesses in C - the tooling you would reach for on a broken sweeper.
Segfault from executing code copied into heap memory; forces reasoning about heap page permissions and layout.
Compile a buggy C program and drive GDB (breakpoints, watchpoints) to the fault; verifier is weak across 36 tests.
Fix the buffer-filling file reader inside a BF interpreter; interpreter plus buffer-sizing bug, small scale.
Write a self-interpreting language and stage it; teaches what bootstrapping means, which the TB task's build depends on.
OCaml let rec versus let shadowing; only real OCaml-language exposure here, but nothing about the runtime.
Diagnose cc1plus missing and repair the toolchain so builds work; the environment-repair skill before any compiler bootstrap.
Implement a C ring buffer with head/tail index arithmetic; index bookkeeping, but implement-from-spec rather than repair.

CalibForge.reason: Mark-and-sweep GC in a C Lisp interpreter segfaults only on memory-heavy programs - the same bug class, language and runtime role as the OCaml sweeper.
Author refactored Lua's memory management and the suite now fails inconsistently; identical premise, including the flaky-failure diagnosis.
Self-inflicted regression in the Lua 5.4.7 interpreter: build with make, run the test suite, find the crash - same loop, strong verifier.
Implicit free list with boundary tags mis-splitting blocks; free-list block accounting is precisely what the OCaml change broke.
Pool allocator with block coalescing crashes under allocation stress - coalescing adjacent free runs is the OCaml sweeper's job.
Refactor to the 9cc C compiler's liveness analysis segfaults make test; broke-my-own-compiler, fix it, same verification route.
Lua code-generator regression that only bites specific expressions; narrow reproduction inside a language implementation.
Explicit free list with boundary-tag coalescing over a static heap - the nearest thing in the pool to compressing free space in a major heap.
Pool allocator silently corrupts messages and crashes after long use; latent corruption that only shows downstream, like a bad sweep.
Implement mark-and-sweep GC in C against a fixed API; teaches the algorithm itself, but as implement-from-spec not repair.

final_top10.reason: Mark-and-sweep GC in a C interpreter crashes only under memory pressure; same runtime, same bug class, same debug loop.
I refactored the interpreter's memory management and the test suite broke - the TB2.1 premise almost verbatim, in Lua.
Self-introduced Lua interpreter regression; build with make, run the suite, isolate the crashing construct. Strong verifier.
Boundary-tag implicit free list mis-splits blocks; free-list bookkeeping is exactly what the OCaml sweeping change corrupted.
Coalescing pool allocator crashes intermittently under stress - run-merging free blocks, reproduced only at scale.
My compiler refactor segfaults make test: fix a self-inflicted regression in a C compiler and get its suite green.
Out-of-bounds write that only manifests at -O2; the optimisation-sensitive memory bug a hand-edited GC produces. Strong tests.
Explicit free list with boundary-tag coalescing over a fixed heap - nearest analogue to compressing free space in the major heap.
Lua codegen regression reproducible only on specific expressions; narrow the failing construct inside a language implementation.
Fix the broken Makefile, then find the memory bug that crashes the C binary on a malformed input - the build-then-debug sequence.

notes: CalibForge dominates this task outright: it holds C-interpreter GC bugs, Lua regressions and four separate free-list/coalescing allocator tasks, all graded ok or better. The v1 pool has essentially no OCaml (search found four OCaml tasks total, all QCheck build exercises) and no GC-internals task at all, so Terminal-Lego and CalibForge both beat the old corpora here. TerminalWorld could not field 10 defensible candidates - its two best matches (tw_245032, tw_226228) are FREE and ranks 8-10 are build boilerplate. Recursive-Task-Synthesis is all absent-verifier and its only OCaml entries are ocamlbuild hello-world builds. SWE-Smith and SWE-Rebench have no C-runtime content; their entries are ranked on toolchain/compiler domain and reclamation-bookkeeping skill only, and should not be expected to carry weight in a merge.
